text:
cate: Heads-up: small sample app repro for a weird POST duplicate after token refresh on device. Not seeing infinite retry, just two POSTs hitting backend.

juan: Which HTTP client and versions? Any custom SDK bits?

cate: Our SDK (kotlin) wraps Retrofit 2.9 + OkHttp 4.11. Authenticator does a blocking refresh and returns request.newBuilder().header(Authorization, ...). No explicit clone() anywhere.

mike: Brief repro steps?

cate: 1) Start local stub that returns 401 then 200. 2) Hit POST /checkout from app (FormBody, ~1KB). 3) Observe two POSTs within ~80ms. Happens on Pixel 6 Android 13 and emulator.

anya: Snippet?

cate: ```kotlin
class TokenAuthenticator: Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    synchronized(this) {
      val newToken = tokenStore.refreshBlocking() // does HTTP call
      return response.request.newBuilder()
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken")
        .build()
    }
  }
}
```

juan: Two likely causes: 1) OkHttp retries buffered bodies on a new connection; 2) Auth refresh code triggers a secondary request that causes the original stream to be forwarded by some proxy.

mike: Also check if your POST body is marked repeatable (FormBody is replayable). OkHttp will resend if it thinks safe. If server is behind a proxy/loadbalancer, you can get duplicate delivery.

cate: Logs show conn ids and different stream ids:
```
[client] POST /checkout id=xyz conn=A stream=3
[server] 401 for id=xyz
[auth] refreshing token...
[client] replay POST /checkout id=xyz conn=B stream=1
[server] 200 for id=xyz
[server] also saw original POST forwarded later on conn=A stream=4
```

anya: Try these experiments: 1) make body non-repeatable (streaming) and repro again; 2) add idempotency-key header to dedupe; 3) single-flight refresh so only one refresh executes.

cate: We have single-flight guard in tokenStore already but still see dups. Switching to a non-buffered RequestBody made duplicates disappear in local run.

juan: That suggests OkHttp is replaying buffered body across connections. Could be exacerbated by HTTP/2 multiplexing + backend proxy. We should: a) document this behavior in SDK FAQ; b) recommend use of idempotency keys for mutating endpoints; c) consider marking our internal retry policy to not retry on 401-handled flows for non-idempotent methods.

mike: Note: Retrofit coroutine adapter had an old bug where calls could be re-enqueued if cancellation raced with authenticate. But that's rare. Consider testing with plain Call.enqueue() sample to rule adapter-influence out.

ci-bot: Quick note: artifact redwood-sdk-snapshots 0.14.2-okhttp4.12 available (contains opt-in okhttp bump).

cate: I'll attach a tiny repro (no prod secrets) and toss it in the repro repo. If non-buffered body fixes it, we should update onboarding sample app to use idempotency header + a note on Authenticator interactions.

anya: Also test on older Androids (11) - networking stacks / carrier proxies sometimes behave differently. I can run smoke matrix on device lab.

juan: If we make a small SDK change, ensure we add an integration test that simulates proxy forwarding to catch regressions.

cate: Thanks folks, will open a PR with repro and patch to sample app. Will ping when CI runs. :rocket:
